options: Exposing WHAT something does while hiding HOW
explanation: car.Start() exposes an intention; the fuel pump, starter motor and ignition stay hidden. Choosing that simple view is abstraction.

stem: Abstraction vs encapsulation - which is right?
options: Abstraction chooses the simple view; encapsulation enforces it with private fields and methods
Encapsulation is about design; abstraction is about fields
explanation: Abstraction is the DESIGN idea (what to expose); encapsulation is the MECHANISM (private state, guarded access). One chooses, the other enforces.

stem: Why can you not write 'new PaymentMethod()' when PaymentMethod is abstract?
options: Its abstract members have no bodies - there is nothing to run
explanation: An abstract class is a partly-finished blueprint. Only concrete subclasses that supply the missing bodies can be instantiated.

stem: public abstract string Pay(decimal amount); - what does this force?
options: Every concrete subclass MUST provide its own Pay body
explanation: abstract = declared with no body. Each concrete child must override it - the base defines WHAT, each child defines HOW.

stem: player.Attack(goblin) sits above sprite.Animate() sits above DrawTriangle(). What is this an example of?
options: Layers of abstraction - each offers a simpler view of the one below
explanation: Layered abstraction is how something as complex as a computer stays comprehensible: each level ignores the details of the one beneath.

stem: list.Sort() hides the algorithm - until 10 million items make you care. This is called:
explanation: An abstraction leaks when the hidden details start to matter anyway. None are perfect; good ones are right almost all the time.

stem: Which public surface shows the RIGHT level of abstraction?
explanation: One clear intention. The first makes the caller do the engine's job; the second says too little; the last exposes internals.

stem: In an abstract class, what is the difference between an abstract method and a virtual one?
options: abstract has no body and MUST be overridden; virtual has a default that MAY be replaced
explanation: abstract = pure requirement. virtual = default offered. A class mixing both defines what every child does, sharing code where it can.

stem: PaymentMethod has a normal Receipt() method with a body. What do subclasses get?
options: Receipt() inherited free - written once, shared by all
explanation: Non-abstract members of an abstract class are ordinary inherited code - the 'some what, some how' that distinguishes abstract classes from interfaces.

options: It is in the System namespace
You print text with no idea how it reaches the screen
explanation: You rely on the WHAT (text appears) with the HOW (buffers, OS calls, rendering) fully hidden - abstraction you have used since lesson 1.1.
